evidence_set: In one patch trial in people with cardiovascular disease (Joseph 1996) there was no evidence that serious adverse events were more common with the patch, and cardiovascular events such as worse angina (about 16% of participants) did not differ by arm. Six trials in pregnant women did not detect significant increases in serious adverse events. A network meta-analysis the review cites (Mills 2014) found more cardiovascular events with NRT than with placebo overall, driven by lower-level events; its figures are quoted from another review and were not checked.

Combination against single form: serious adverse events RR 4.44 (0.76 to 25.85), 5 studies, 2,888 participants, seven events in total, 1 per 1,000 with a single form against 3 per 1,000 (1 to 18) with combination, low certainty (two levels for imprecision); any cardiac event RR 0.66 (0.22 to 2.05; 2 studies; 656); withdrawals due to treatment RR 1.12 (0.57 to 2.20; 5 studies; 3,070; I² 73%), 12 per 1,000 with a single form against 14 with combination, very low certainty. Only 3 of the 16 combination trials reported cardiac events; Piper 2009 (1,504 participants) reported 32 serious events not split by arm.

Fast-acting forms against the patch: withdrawals due to treatment RR 4.23 (1.54 to 11.63), 3 studies, 1,482 participants, 5 per 1,000 with the patch against 23 per 1,000 (8 to 63) with fast-acting forms, very low certainty; nasal spray against patch RR 3.47 (1.15 to 10.46), 1 study, 922, 3.0% against 0.9%. Serious events: three of four studies had none (1,252 participants in all four); the fourth RR 1.75 (0.52 to 5.92; 642 participants); very low certainty. Cardiac events reported by arm in one small trial: none in either arm.

evidence_set: Against NRT: use of the allocated product at six months or longer was reported by 5 trials (none at high risk of bias; one, Russell 2021, industry-funded) and could not be pooled (I² 95%); in 3 trials more people in the vape arm kept using it than in the NRT arm, in 2 (Russell 2021, Lee 2018) there was no difference. Five trials (counted separately in the text: none industry-funded, one high risk) reported long-term product patterns: vaping without smoking RR 4.40 (1.27 to 15.28), I² 78%, 2,776 participants; abstinence from both vaping and smoking RR 0.49 (0.26 to 0.91), I² 31%, 2,776; concurrent vaping and smoking higher in the vape arm in 3 of 4 trials (not pooled); smoking without vaping RR 0.76 (0.58 to 1.01), I² 83%, 4 trials, 2,543. Absolute counts are in forest plots that were not read.
